entries.acceptance: After the breath interval spend one fatigue per second; at zero fatigue require a will check each second to avoid unconsciousness and apply the suffocation procedure.

Standing broad-jump distance in feet is twice basic movement minus three; a running start adds its yards before evaluation, with distance capped at twice standing distance.
With a running start, enhanced ground movement multiplies movement before the jumping formulas instead of also adding run-up yards.
Each enhanced-jump level doubles final jump distance, cumulatively with enhanced movement where applicable.
Full combat jump distance requires two consecutive concentration maneuvers; an unprepared jump has half distance.
A small-obstacle combat jump uses a movement maneuver and costs one additional movement point.
Jumping a larger obstacle or onto a surface uses the whole movement turn; vertical and long horizontal jumps require a dexterity check when specified by the hazard.
A failed difficult jump leaves the actor fallen and requires two posture changes to stand; critical failure invokes falling damage from the actual height.
Clambering onto a vertical obstacle with two consecutive movement maneuvers avoids the risky dexterity roll; validate the route and reachable obstacle before committing.

When explicitly enabled, multiply distance by the encumbrance factor 1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4 or 0.2; do not assume this optional reduction in the baseline formulas.

entries.acceptance: Keep mass invariant under gravity changes; derive local weight separately for encumbrance and lifting.
Gravity below 0.1G is microgravity; zero gravity is a distinct movement condition and must not divide formulas by zero.

Above one gravity, add (body weight plus gear weight) times (local gravity minus one) to ordinary carried gear weight; 150-pound body plus 30-pound gear at 1.2G yields effective encumbrance 66 pounds.
Below one gravity, multiply gear weight by local gravity for encumbrance; reduced body weight affects jumping but is not a negative carried load.
Without flight or another movement aid, zero-gravity movement requires pushing off a solid surface and proceeds at floor(strength/2) until contact or another applicable force changes it.
Scale ordinary jumping distances by one divided by local gravity, except the running-start bonus to high-jump height; if distance at least doubles, use enhanced-jump bounding movement rules.
Scale throwing distance by one divided by local gravity but leave damage based on mass, not locally reduced weight.
Scale terminal velocity by local gravity and resolve resulting falls through the hazard rules.
Apply free-fall skill and dexterity rules in zero gravity, except beam weapons with recoil below two and vehicles or tools designed for zero gravity.
Use home gravity and the actor's tolerance increment, normally 0.2G; count full increments of difference by rounding down with stable threshold arithmetic.
Apply -1 dexterity per full increment for agility and ballistic tasks, or -1 per two full increments with relevant gravity experience; do not apply it to beam weapons or lock manipulation.
Higher gravity imposes -1 intelligence per two full increments; lower gravity imposes no corresponding intelligence penalty.
Higher gravity imposes -1 health and -1 fatigue capacity per two full increments; lower gravity does not grant a bonus. Route temporary-score effects through health rules.
Ordinary objects up to eight times lifting capacity may be thrown; ready them first, use one hand only up to twice capacity, and use an attack maneuver in combat.
Ordinary object accuracy is dexterity-3 against a specific target or dexterity for a general area, with applicable size, speed and range modifiers.

Divide object weight by lifting capacity, select the next higher table ratio at an in-between value, then multiply strength by the corresponding distance factor. Table rows above ordinary lift eligibility do not waive the weight limit.
Base damage on strength thrust and the weight-band adjustment; use crushing unless an authored shape supports cutting, piercing or impaling.
A fragile thrown object or thrown character also takes damage, rolled independently from damage to its target.
Throwing skill can replace accuracy for palm-sized objects; relative skill +1 adds one strength for range, and relative +2 or higher adds two.
The cinematic throwing skill can throw any eligible object; at relative level zero add one strength for range and one damage per die, increasing both bonuses to two at relative +1 or better.
Purpose-built thrown weapons use their own weapon skills, ranges and damage instead of ordinary-object formulas, with the cinematic throwing-skill exception.

An intentional successful area lob may be caught using dexterity or suitable sport skill, at -4 without waiting and +1 per two full points of thrower success margin; it counts as a parry with the catching hand.
Intercepting an object en route to someone else uses a thrown-weapon parry; success captures the object and updates its ownership/position once.

Extra effort is unavailable to mechanical bodies and cannot extend breath holding; declare the specific supported physical quantity being increased.
Roll will at -1 per five-percent increase and an additional penalty equal to fatigue already missing; authorized fear, anger or concern may grant +5.
Use a will-based relevant physical skill instead of will when better, preserving that skill's investment and the task-specific effort procedure.
Ordinary extra effort costs one fatigue per attempt or interval after its roll, whether successful or failed; that newly spent fatigue does not penalize the same roll.
Success grants the selected physical increase but does not guarantee the underlying task succeeds; critical success waives the effort fatigue cost.
Ordinary failure yields only baseline capability; critical failure fails the task and inflicts health injury equal to all fatigue spent on the attempt, including its ordinary task cost.
A natural eighteen additionally requires immediate health resolution for a task-appropriate temporary impairment, using crippling-duration rules that can make it permanent.
Digging checks effort hourly and adds one fatigue to the normal work cost; critical injury affects the back and heals by rest rather than first aid, with the natural-eighteen back impairment rule.
Hiking checks once daily and adds two fatigue to the stop penalty; critical injury is assessed at day end from that modified fatigue amount.
A single will-based hiking effort roll includes the ordinary twenty-percent hiking bonus, with -1 per additional five percent; do not also roll ordinary hiking for another bonus.
Effort improves final jumping distance rather than basic movement; critical injury affects a foot or leg and natural eighteen risks a crippled leg.
Continuing lifting effort checks once per minute and adds one fatigue; will-based lifting uses -1 per ten-percent extra capacity instead of the ordinary five-percent-per-margin bonus.
Check effort each fifteen sprint seconds or paced minute and add its fatigue to any ordinary failed endurance-check cost; critical injury affects a leg.
Check effort each swimming minute and add one fatigue in addition to ordinary failed swimming-endurance costs.
Effort strength affects throw range and damage but not the initial permissible lift; lifting effort is a separate attempt, and skill bonuses apply after effort strength.
Combat effort is an explicit campaign option and uses its own procedure rather than the ordinary will-based effort roll.
Declare effort and pay its fatigue before the attack or defense roll; invalid combinations must be rejected before payment.
Critical failure adds one injury to the used arm or leg, ignoring armor, in addition to ordinary critical effects.
Except during an all-out attack, one fatigue grants +2 to one active defense, including offsetting a repeated-parry penalty.
With an attack maneuver, pay one fatigue per attack to halve its rapid-strike penalty.
With a melee attack maneuver, pay one fatigue per attack for the strong all-out-attack damage bonus while retaining defenses.
The rapid-attack and strong-attack effort options cannot be combined on the same use.
